decisions.thought: Plan: Bring Mega Dragonite sweeper, Scarf Gholdengo revenge, Rotom-Wash wall for Garchomp/Dragonite. Rotom burns physical threats, pivots to Dragonite to setup, Gholdengo cleans. No Grass/Dragon coverage so Rotom mirror needs Trick/Taunt pressure.

decisions.thought:
Brought Garchomp (lead), Gholdengo (Scarf), Kingambit. Garchomp: Swords Dance or EQ. Gholdengo: revenge-kill / Trick. Kingambit: late-game cleaner with Sucker Punch.
Watch for their Volcarona (Quiver Dance) and their Dragonite (Dragon Dance). Their Rotom-Wash may burn my physical attackers.
Lead Rotom vs Garchomp good: immune EQ. Plan: burn Garchomp with Wisp to cripple, then Hydro pressure, pivot to Dragonite to setup, keep Gholdengo scarf to revenge. Watch for Mega Garchomp/Dragonite.

decisions.thought: Garchomp Mega'd T1, Dragon Clawing Rotom-Wash (Levitate, EQ useless). If Garchomp gets burned, switch to Gholdengo (Good as Gold blocks status); Trick Scarf onto Rotom is an option. Kingambit is the late cleaner with Sucker Punch. Watch for Volcarona/Dragonite setup. Log Rotom's moves and speed.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Thinking through Rotom-Wash against Garchomp — Levitate makes it immune to Earthquake, but Garchomp outspeeds and Mega Garchomp's boosted Attack is threatening. I'm weighing whether Will-O-Wisp, Hydro Pump, or a switch to something like Kingambit is the better play here.

Gholdengo looks appealing as a switch since its Good as Gold ability blocks status like WoW entirely, and it's neutral to Hydro Pump and Volt Switch. I could even consider Trick to cripple Rotom with the scarf, though that costs me speed control on Gholdengo. Running the numbers on Mega Garchomp's Dragon Claw, it does roughly 50% to offensive Rotom builds or around 37% to bulkier ones, so Rotom likely responds with Will-O-Wisp. Ultimately I'll just mega evolve and go with Dragon Claw now since it's reliable compared to the riskier 80%-accuracy Stone Edge.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Garchomp is now burned, with Dragon Claw dealing 37% while unhurt and the burn tick bringing it down roughly 18% more. Rotom sits at 63%, so I'm weighing switching to Gholdengo or using a scarf Make It Rain, checking that Steel-type move's effectiveness against Rotom's typing before deciding, since Water/Electric resist it heavily while Shadow Ball stays neutral.

Shadow Ball from Gholdengo should chunk Rotom for roughly 40% per hit, meaning two hits finishes it off, and Trick onto Rotom would cripple it by locking it into a scarfed move like Will-O-Wisp. Since burned Garchomp isn't doing much useful work anymore, switching into Gholdengo looks like the better line here.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to reconsider the speed comparison—Gholdengo's 149 is its raw stat, but with Choice Scarf it jumps to 223, which outpaces Rotom's 151. That changes the matchup calculus: Shadow Ball from Rotom would deal around 40% per hit, but if Gholdengo moves first with a scarf, it could use Trick or another move before taking that damage.

Tricking the scarf onto Rotom would lock it into whatever move it commits to—risky if it's Hydro Pump but potentially useful if it gets stuck on something weaker like Will-O-Wisp. Switching to Kingambit is another option since Hydro Pump is only neutral against it, though the burn chance is a concern.

Running the damage numbers, Shadow Ball twice should be enough to take down Rotom, and Gholdengo can likely survive the return Hydro Pump unless there's an unlucky high roll. I'll go with Shadow Ball as the safer, more direct line.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Gholdengo is locked into Shadow Ball with Dragonite at 78% and Multiscale already broken, speed lowered by one stage, suggesting Dragon Dance or Extreme Speed/Earthquake coverage incoming. Shadow Ball would only do about 22% to Dragonite, so I'm weighing whether switching to Kingambit is the safer play.

Dragonite could carry Extreme Speed, Earthquake, Fire Punch, or Dragon Dance, and Kingambit resists most of that while Garchomp's burned Dragon Claw would only net around 55-60% without the KO. If I stay with Gholdengo it likely dies to Earthquake and sets up Kingambit's Supreme Overlord boost, or I could sack Garchomp first to chip Dragonite down before bringing in a cleaner finisher.

Sticking with Shadow Ball now seems best: it drops Gholdengo's HP from 78% to roughly 56%, and if it survives I keep attacking, while if it faints I can bring in Garchomp for a likely KO with Dragon Claw.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Rotom-Wash is at 66% after Sitrus kicked in, with Dragon Claw dealing 24% and Stone Edge threatening around 30% at 80% accuracy, though neither move secures a KO. I'm weighing whether switching to Kingambit is risky given Will-O-Wisp potential, while Garchomp sits comfortably at 88%.

Running the math on Swords Dance lines: even boosted, two Dragon Claws or two Stone Edges don't cleanly break through Rotom's HP, and Hydro Pump recoil on Garchomp (factoring burn) could leave it dead before it lands a second hit. The sequencing matters a lot here -- if Garchomp attacks first each turn but Rotom's Hydro Pump plus burn damage outpaces its own offense, I need to find a turn order where Garchomp either finishes Rotom off or switches out before taking the fatal hit.

Simplifying: just attacking with Dragon Claw is the safer, more consistent choice over Stone Edge, since Stone Edge's crit chance isn't reliable enough to offset its lower accuracy-adjusted damage. That whittles Rotom down to around 18%, setting up Kingambit to clean up afterward -- though I need to account for Rotom's Volt Switch possibility and Dragonite's speed advantage against Kingambit if it switches in. I'm now checking whether Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave, boosted by Supreme Overlord and Black Glasses, can secure a solid chunk of damage on Rotom to make this plan work.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Dragonite at 17% and moving first as Mega, I'm checking if Earthquake can take down Kingambit at 171 HP - estimating Mega Dragonite's attack around 193, the hit lands for roughly 62 damage, not enough to finish it off.

Sucker Punch fails against Roost or Dragon Dance, but Kowtow Cleave with burn and +2 Overlord boost should reliably KO Dragonite's 17% health regardless of what it does, since even a post-Roost hit does solid damage. The real question is whether Dragonite's Earthquake plus a crit could kill Kingambit first, but that seems unlikely enough that Kowtow Cleave is the safer, more decisive play.

decisions.thought: Kingambit is my last: burned, Black Glasses, Supreme Overlord +2. Using Swords Dance now. Unboosted Cleave does about 32% to their Mega Dragonite (35%, Multiscale, has Roost and Earthquake, faster). At +2, Cleave does about 64%. If Dragonite attacks, Sucker Punch to KO. If it Roosts, Cleave or a second Swords Dance. Avoid letting it reach full HP (Multiscale).
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Dragonite's at 35%, and Cleave only did about 32% last turn, so it likely won't KO this time either. If Roost heals it back up to around 85%, the next Cleave would only bring it to roughly 53%, so this could turn into a stalling loop unless something changes.

Weighing other options: Sucker Punch is weaker than Cleave, Iron Head is also weaker without a damage boost, and Swords Dance would double Cleave's output but still might not KO if Dragonite roosts back to 85% first. Dragonite also threatens Earthquake, which is super effective on Kingambit's Steel typing, so there's real risk in giving it a free turn. The burn reducing physical damage complicates the math too -- betting on Cleave rolling high enough to KO at 35% feels like the gamble to consider.

Looking at the long game, Swords Dance scales better if Dragonite keeps roosting: at +2 Cleave gets to roughly 64%, at +4 it's well over 100%, enough to break through Multiscale and burn chip. Even if Dragonite attacks instead of rooting, Sucker Punch and Cleave without boosts don't KO, so I'm not losing much by setting up. I'll go with Swords Dance.

Dragonite's at 85%, no Multiscale since it's not full health, and Kingambit is still +2 after the burn. Unboosted Last Resort did about 32%, so a +2 hit would land around 64%, not quite lethal from 85%. If Cleave drops it to roughly 21%, it might try Roost to heal back up rather than risk staying low.

Since Kingambit outspeeds, if it Roosts first to full health Multiscale kicks back in, halving my damage—meaning I'd need another Swords Dance to push through at +4 or higher to break through that cushion even with the burn chipping it each turn.
